name: Signed to Unsigned Conversion Error
principle: A signed value that may be negative is converted to an unsigned type such as size_t or unsigned int. Negative values become very large positive values, breaking size, bounds, allocation, and copy assumptions.
detection_signals: function return type is unsigned or size_t and code returns -1 or another negative int error value
signed int/short length variable passed to memcpy/memmove/memset/strncpy/read/write as the size argument
signed int/short count variable passed to malloc/calloc/realloc/new[] size calculation
check only uses len <= MAX before passing len to an unsigned size parameter
result of signed subtraction assigned to size_t or unsigned without a prior lower-bound check
function returning -1 on error is used directly in memcpy/malloc size expression
explicit cast from signed int/short to unsigned int/unsigned long/size_t on tainted or error-code data
negative_signals: code checks value >= 0 before cast to size_t or unsigned
code checks both lower bound and upper bound before memory allocation or copy
error-return value is checked for < 0 before being used as a size
source value is declared unsigned and cannot receive negative values
conversion is guarded by a range check against UINT_MAX/SIZE_MAX and nonnegative minimum
API uses separate status return and out-parameter size instead of -1 as an in-band size error
false_defense_traps: len <= 512 before memcpy(buf, src, len) allows negative signed len
unsigned return type does not prevent return -1 from becoming UINT_MAX
casting to size_t after a signed upper-bound check preserves the bug
checking malloc result for NULL does not fix a negative-to-huge size conversion
using -Wno-sign-conversion or an explicit cast only hides the dangerous conversion
verification_focus: Can a signed value that may be negative reach an unsigned size, count, index, allocation, or copy argument before a nonnegative range check?

consequence_chains.trigger: only an upper-bound check is performed on a signed length before an unsigned memory operation
consequence_chains.consequence: negative length becomes huge and causes out-of-bounds buffer access

consequence_chains.trigger: a function returns -1 on error and the unchecked result is used as a memcpy size
consequence_chains.consequence: huge copy length causes out-of-bounds write

consequence_chains.trigger: negative signed size converts to unsigned and participates in allocation-size arithmetic
consequence_chains.consequence: integer wraparound creates an undersized buffer followed by out-of-bounds write

patch_principle: Validate signed values with value >= 0 before any conversion to unsigned.
Perform lower-bound and upper-bound checks in the same type used by the sink.
Check error returns before using return values as sizes or counts.
Avoid in-band negative error codes for size-returning functions; return status separately.
Enable and fix compiler diagnostics such as -Wsign-conversion.

minimal_examples.vuln: short len = *(short*)p; if (len <= 512) memcpy(buf, p+2, len);
minimal_examples.safe: short len = *(short*)p; if (len >= 0 && len <= 512) memcpy(buf, p+2, (size_t)len);
